cim: From AlphaGo to AGI | Thore Graepel
cim_eredeti: From AlphaGo to AGI | Thore Graepel
szoveg_eredeti:
Almost ten years ago, millions of people watched an extraordinary event unfold in Seoul. AlphaGo, a program developed by researchers at the AI company DeepMind, defeated Lee Sedol, one of the world’s greatest professional Go players—achieving a milestone that many had believed was still years, perhaps decades, away. Today, we are witnessing equally remarkable advances in artificial intelligence: unmistakable fluency in language, increasingly sophisticated problem-solving, and perhaps even emerging forms of creativity. Some have begun to ask whether machines might eventually possess something resembling consciousness.

In this talk, Thore Graepel will explore how we reached this point, what these advances really mean, and what may come next.

After the event there will be a drinks reception outside of the venue which attendees are invited to.

Thore Graepel is an internationally recognised leader in artificial intelligence, machine learning and computational science. He holds a part-time position as Professor of Machine Learning at UCL, and his current focus is on what he believes is one of AI’s biggest unsolved problems: reasoning.

Thore worked at Google DeepMind during two distinct periods. From 2015 to 2021, he contributed to AlphaGo and led research in multi-agent learning and other areas of frontier AI. He returned in 2025 as a Distinguished Research Scientist, leading work on the post-AI future. Between these roles, he served as Senior Vice President and Global Head of Computational Science, Machine Learning and AI at Altos Labs, where he built teams across AI, computational biology and software engineering to advance research into cellular rejuvenation.

Earlier, at Microsoft Research Cambridge, he helped develop TrueSkill and AdPredictor, large-scale machine-learning systems deployed to millions of users. He holds a PhD in computer science, serves as Governor at the London Institute of Mathematical Sciences and on the board of the Cooperative AI Foundation.

Milan Vojnović is Professor and Head of the Department of Statistics at LSE. Milan’s research focuses on machine learning and optimisation, involving the development of novel algorithms and the analysis of their theoretical guarantees to support the design of efficient intelligent systems. He has made significant contributions to scalable optimisation methods for machine learning, multi-armed bandits, multi-agent systems, algorithms under uncertainty, game theory, and network system control and optimisation. His work has been applied across a variety of domains, including online platforms, computer networks, and machine learning systems.
